Done. The export is written under `out/T3/` and the self-report is in place.

**What the script does** (`out/T3/solution.py`): loads both input shards, casts only tensors matching an anchored regex for the seven per-layer projection weights to bfloat16, keeps everything else float32 and untouched, runs the required checks (112 bf16, layer-0 q_proj bf16, embed_tokens float32, 114 tensors, unchanged names and shapes), then packs shards greedily in original key order with a 256 MiB budget and writes the index file.

**Result:**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Shards written | 10 |
| Tensors in weight_map | 114 |
| bfloat16 tensors | 112 |
| Oversized solo shards | 2 (embed_tokens, lm_head) |

**Executions:** two. The first run failed on my own sanity check, which flagged the 412 MB single-tensor shard as over budget before any file was written. I qualified that check to apply only to multi-tensor shards and the second run succeeded.

The self-report at `out/T3/REPORT.md` records the two executions, the pitfall, and the unspecified shard-naming convention, for which I used the HuggingFace `model-XXXXX-of-NNNNN.safetensors` pattern.
